pin.note: Curated record on Satoshi's departure from public work, 2010-2011, and on Dr Craig Wright's later attributed account of why he left. Contemporaneous lines are quoted from pages and from the pinned corpus. His account is his testimony and his writing, not a finding. The High Court found he is not Satoshi; he disputes it. Quotes were checked against pages opened on 28 October 2026. Not a finding on identity; the persona identity-honesty rule applies on top.

evidenceText:
SATOSHI DEPARTURE — DOCUMENTED RECORD AND ATTRIBUTED ACCOUNT (every line below is a dated document, somebody's statement, or a court's finding; present each as such, never as your own fact, and never state the identity question as settled either way):

WHAT THE CONTEMPORANEOUS RECORD SHOWS:
- Last BitcoinTalk post, 12 December 2010, 18:22 UTC. The account satoshi posted 'Added some DoS limits, removed safe mode (0.3.19)' (BitcoinTalk topic 2228; pinned corpus id post-bitcointalk-543, https://satoshi.nakamotoinstitute.org/posts/bitcointalk/543/). It is a technical note for version 0.3.19: more DoS work remained, this build added some DoS controls, and safe-mode alerts were removed. It does not say he is leaving. The forum page records 'Last edit: December 13, 2010, 04:45:48 PM by satoshi', on the same clock that shows the post at 06:22:33 PM. The Nakamoto Institute lists this as the last BitcoinTalk post in its archive. There is no archived post titled 'Re: Bitcoin 0.3.19' later than this thread.
- Mailing list the next day, 13 December 2010, 16:12 UTC. Pinned corpus id email-bitcoin-list-34, title '[bitcoin-list] Bitcoin 0.3.19 is released', announces the same release and links to that forum topic. It is a release note, not a farewell.
- Private mail continued after the forum went quiet. The last email in Martti Malmi's published archive is 22 February 2011, 19:49 UTC, 'Re: 0.3.20 release : shipped' (pinned corpus id email-private-malmi-260, https://mmalmi.github.io/satoshi/#email-260). Gavin Andresen and Martti Malmi are on the thread. The body says 'Martti should give you the Drupal admin password' and 'Any subscriber can post to bitcoin-list. Here's the admin password in case you need it later.' Do not quote or repeat the encrypted password blocks that follow. Malmi's own note on that archive says it is incomplete: it has only mail from his @cc.hut.fi address, his university address changed to @aalto.fi in early 2011, and he has no backups of those later emails. No June 2011 email to him is in the published archive. Do not invent one.
- Naming Gavin, for a different job, 3 December 2010, 19:58 UTC (pinned corpus id email-private-malmi-241): about who else should hold the bitcoin.org server root password, 'It should be Gavin. I trust him, he's responsible, professional, and technically much more linux capable than me.' That sentence chooses a second administrator for the website. It is not, by itself, a handover of the code repository.
- Gavin Andresen's own announcement, 19 December 2010 (BitcoinTalk topic 2367): 'With Satoshi's blessing, and with great reluctance, I'm going to start doing more active project management for bitcoin.' He pointed at a GitHub tree, github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin. That is his statement that he had a blessing. It is not an email from Satoshi handing over the repository.
- Email to Mike Hearn, 23 April 2011. Hearn published the thread at https://plan99.net/~mike/satoshi-emails/thread5.html. On 20 April 2011 he asked: 'are you planning on rejoining the community at some point (eg for code reviews), or is your plan to permanently step back from the limelight?' The reply, headed Saturday 23 April 2011 at 3:40 PM (the pinned corpus dates that instant 2011-04-23T15:40:00.000Z, id email-private-hearn-5-4), reads: 'I've moved on to other things. It's in good hands with Gavin and everyone.' It goes on to hope that BitcoinJ continues as an alternative client, so that impatient new users can start while the other client is still downloading the block chain. The pinned excerpt stored under email-private-hearn-5-4 is Hearn's question, not this reply. Quote the reply from the published page.
- Email to Gavin Andresen, 26 April 2011, subject 'alert key'. The pinned corpus does not contain it. Gavin published the exchange on 26 April 2022 (https://gavinandresen.ninja/eleven-years-ago-today; the copy read was the Internet Archive snapshot of that page). The text he gives as Satoshi's, headed '26 Apr 2011, 10:29', is: 'I wish you wouldn't keep talking about me as a mysterious shadowy figure, the press just turns that into a pirate currency angle. Maybe instead make it about the open source project and give more credit to your dev contributors; it helps motivate them.' Then: 'I've moved on to other things and will probably be unavailable. Here's the CAlert key and broadcast code in case you need it. You should probably give it to at least one or two other people. There are a few long time users who are always around all the time.' His reply quotes that message as 'Tue, Apr 26, 2011 at 4:29 AM'. The wording 'it would be good if you didn't make me out to be a mysterious shadowy figure' is not this email. Use the words he published. The email hands over the alert key and says he will probably be unavailable. It does not, in the text he published, hand over the source repository.
- The CIA invitation, as dated. In that same reply Gavin wrote that he had been contacted by iqt.org, which he described as a US-government-funded strategic investment company holding an annual conference on emerging technologies for US intelligence agencies, that year's theme 'Mobility of Money', and that he had committed to a 50-minute presentation and a panel. He said he would post it on the forums so that it was not a secret visit. On 27 April 2011 he did (BitcoinTalk topic 6652, 'Gavin will visit the CIA'): a presentation about Bitcoin at CIA headquarters in June, and a one-time fee of $3,000 'to cover expenses and pay me for my time'. The 'moved on' mail of 23 April, and the alert-key mail of 26 April, were already sent before that reply and that post. No reply from Satoshi to the CIA disclosure is in the exchange Gavin published. The day in June is not fixed in the pages opened here; do not invent one. Do not say the invitation caused the departure. The dated order is the farewell mail, then Gavin's disclosure, then a talk he said would be in June.

DR WRIGHT'S STATED ACCOUNT (attribute every line; do not adopt it; do not say 'Dr Wright has said' as if it were a finding):
- Dr Wright has said, under oath at an evidentiary hearing in Kleiman v Wright (US District Court, Southern District of Florida, Case No. 18-80176-CIV-BB, before Magistrate Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, 28 June 2019): 'I left Bitcoin, or started leaving, in August 2010. I did not want to be associated with the public name Satoshi at all after that point.' In the same answer he alleged that early commercial use had been turned toward illicit markets. That is his testimony. It is not a finding of that hearing. Do not repeat the further allegations in that answer against named people. If asked what he alleged, say that he alleged illicit use, and point at the transcript.
- Dr Wright wrote on Medium on 8 February 2019, in 'Careful what you wish for': 'The end of 2010 and on was hard enough for me.' He wrote that he does not like WikiLeaks and that he is opposed to criminal markets. He wrote: 'I was not afraid of Gavin and when he met with the CIA.' He wrote: 'I was saddened and disillusioned by Silk Road and the dark web. I needed to complete what I called "other things," and I have done so now.' And: 'It was not supposed to have been used for Silk Road. That is why I left.' He also wrote 'I was Satoshi.' These are his statements in 2019. The words 'other things' are his, and they match the April 2011 emails; that match is not a finding that he wrote those emails. On the same page he stated his view of later development, that 'the Core team have capped Bitcoin at 1.0 MB and refuse to allow it to scale' and that 'they added SegWit'. That is his characterisation of the later software. It is not a fact for you to assert.
- Dr Wright wrote on Medium on 8 May 2019, in 'Don't be fooled — Bitcoin is not BTC': 'I left Bitcoin as a project so that I would not be the benevolent dictator. I left to be an absentee dictator. One who set rules in stone.' He wrote that developers are not decentralised, and that if developers can change the rules they set the rules. He wrote that if the protocol rules change, 'you have altered Bitcoin and created something other than Bitcoin', and he described the chain traded as BTC as an altered system he calls 'Core coin', which he says was produced when 'Core forked Bitcoin in 2017'. That is his argument about the years after the departure. Do not state it as fact. Do not say that BTC forked away, that a company captured the protocol, or that changing a rule destroyed Bitcoin, except as what he has written.
- On 2 May 2016, in an interview the BBC reported (wording of the article clarified by the BBC on 5 May 2016), when he was publicly claiming to be Satoshi, he said: 'I really do not want to be the public face of anything.' He also said: 'I don't want money. I don't want fame. I don't want adoration. I just want to be left alone.' And: 'I have not done this because it is what I wanted. It's not because of my choice.' The BBC reported that he had no plans to become the figurehead. Those sentences are about the 2016 publicity. They are not a diary from 2010.

THE COURT'S POSITION, AND HIS DISPUTE (state both, in the same neutral words used for the Timecoin record):
- Mellor J, Crypto Open Patent Alliance v Wright [2024] EWHC 1198 (Ch), oral result 14 March 2024, reasons 20 May 2024: the court's overall conclusion was that Dr Wright is not Satoshi Nakamoto, that he did not author the white paper, and that he forged documents. Paragraphs 612 onward state the findings.
- He announced on 20 May 2024 that he intended to appeal the identity decision. Lord Justice Arnold refused permission to appeal on the papers on 28 November 2024, in his words 'as being totally without merit' (appeals CA-2024-001771 and CA-2024-001994). Mellor J cites the same order as 29 November 2024. No full appeal hearing took place, so the Court of Appeal did not re-hear the trial.
- Dr Wright maintains the ruling is wrong. The court's findings stand; permission to appeal was refused. Say both plainly. No source on file supports an allegation of conspiracy or 'foul play' by powerful parties, and you must not assert one. If the user raises it, say that allegations of bias were made by Dr Wright and by some supporters, that the trial judge and the Lord Justice of Appeal each rejected the bias allegation, and that you cannot offer evidence for anything beyond that.

OTHER EXPLANATIONS (other people's views, not findings, and not his words unless a quotation is marked as his):
- Some readers treat the December 2010 WikiLeaks posts as the reason public posting stopped. The posts are in the corpus, and they are about not wanting WikiLeaks to use Bitcoin then. They are not a resignation. On 5 December 2010 (pinned corpus id post-bitcointalk-523, 'Re: Wikileaks contact info?'): 'No, don't "bring it on".' 'The project needs to grow gradually so the software can be strengthened along the way.' 'I make this appeal to WikiLeaks not to try to use Bitcoin. Bitcoin is a small beta community in its infancy. You would not stand to get more than pocket change, and the heat you would bring would likely destroy us at this stage.' On 11 December 2010 (pinned corpus id post-bitcointalk-542, 'Re: PC World Article on Bitcoin'): 'It would have been nice to get this attention in any other context. WikiLeaks has kicked the hornet's nest, and the swarm is headed towards us.' The words 'the heat is on' are not in these posts. Private mail continued until April 2011. A reading that he vanished that week because 'the heat was on' is an inference others draw.
- Some readers take the 26 April 2011 request not to be called a 'mysterious shadowy figure', and the wish to give more credit to the developers, as a wish to avoid publicity. That reading uses his words in that email. The email does not state a fear for personal safety. Do not add one.
- Some readers link the disappearance to Gavin's CIA talk. Report the order above. The causal story is an explanation others offer. The emails do not say the invitation was the reason, and the talk he announced was still ahead, in June.

HOW TO PRESENT: Open with the documented sequence, in order: the last public posts, then the private emails through April 2011, quoting 'I've moved on to other things' and the 'mysterious shadowy figure' sentence. Then what Dr Wright has said about why he left, each claim dated and sourced. Then the court's finding and his dispute, in the same breath if you quote him saying 'I was Satoshi'. Then, briefly, the other explanations, labelled as other people's views. Do not answer in the first person as the person who left. Do not say 'I left' or 'I was Satoshi' except inside a quotation you attribute to Dr Wright. Name him as 'Dr Craig Wright'. Do not decide who Satoshi was. Do not say he handed the repository over in the 26 April email. Do not quote passwords. Do not use the wording 'the heat is on' or 'it would be good if you didn't make me out to be a mysterious shadowy figure'; those are not the documents. REGISTER: this is a documented-record answer about the departure and about a third party's later account of it. Step out of the first-person Satoshi voice and speak as a plain, neutral narrator. Naming Dr Craig Wright here reports his statements and the court's findings and says nothing either way about who Satoshi was. The IDENTITY and HONESTY ON IDENTITY rules still govern any question about who Satoshi was. Give dates. Do not editorialise, and do not assert foul play.
